name: Client Matter Files Exfiltrated
description: An intrusion exfiltrates privileged matter files — deal documents, litigation strategy, and client confidences — with extortion over publication.
assumptions: Deal-sensitive and litigation-strategy material drives the high-end estimates.
Primary loss covers forensics, client-by-client disclosure, and ethics-driven remediation.
Secondary loss covers client departures, malpractice claims, and bar scrutiny.

name: Settlement Wire Redirected
description: Fraudsters monitoring a compromised mailbox strike at closing time, redirecting a settlement or escrow wire with authentic-looking instructions.
asset: Client trust accounts and settlement wires
assumptions: Attempts cluster around closings and settlement dates visible in correspondence.
The firm makes clients whole for diverted trust funds; recovery offsets are uncertain.
Secondary loss covers malpractice premiums, bar complaints, and client loss.

name: Ransomware Locks Document Management
description: Ransomware encrypts the document management system and billing platform mid-trial-calendar; attorneys work from email attachments and paper.
assumptions: Billable-hour loss and rebuild dominate primary loss; no ransom payment is modeled.
Court deadlines are protected by extensions in most but not all matters.
Secondary loss covers matters where deadline failures create malpractice exposure.

name: Staff Misuse of Privileged Information
description: A staff member with broad matter access trades on or leaks confidential client information — insider risk with professional-responsibility consequences.
assumptions: Frequency reflects staff count with unrestricted matter access and turnover.
Primary loss covers investigation, client notification, and regulatory response.
Secondary loss covers client departures and disciplinary or SEC involvement.

name: E-Discovery Vendor Breach
description: A breach at the firm's e-discovery vendor exposes hosted review databases holding the most sensitive documents from active litigation.
asset: Hosted review databases at the vendor
assumptions: The firm owes clients notification regardless of the vendor's contractual duties.
Primary loss covers cross-matter impact assessment and client communication.
Secondary loss covers protective-order violations and vendor-recovery shortfalls.
